newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kinkel says in favour of fully privatising Telekom.
newsitem.headline: Kinkel says in favour of fully privatising Telekom.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel believes Bonn should consider selling off the full balance of its 74 percent stake in German telephone monopoly Deutsche Telekom AG, a German newspaper said on Thursday.

Handelsblatt quoted Kinkel as saying in an interview that he would not rule such a move as part of Bonn's efforts to meet entry criteria for the single European currency, which is slated to begin in January 1999.

"There is still more with Telekom," Kinkel , a member of Germany's Free Democratic party, was quoted as saying. The newspaper put out a press release ahead of the publication of the interview in its Friday edition.

"I would have nothing against the rest being privatised," said Kinkel, whose party is junior partner in Chancellor Helmut Kohl's ruling coalition with the Christian Democrats and Christian Social Union.

Finance Minister Theo Waigel said last week Bonn was considering an early sale of additional shares in Telekom this year but said it would not help Germany meet deficit target criteria for entry into the single currency.

Instead, Waigel said the proceeds of his plan, which has drawn criticism since Bonn is obliged under law not to sell any more shares on stock exchanges before the year 2000, would be used to pay off old debt.
Bonn has not said what portion of its 74 percent stake of Telekom's 2.7 billion shares, which is valued at about 80 billion marks at current market prices, would be sold.
Industry analysts believe any sale of Telekom shares by Bonn would be done through a private placement to institutional investors.
